newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 65-75 bcf in weekly AGA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 65-75 bcf in weekly AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 65-75 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged widely from 20-85 bcf for the week ended Nov 15.
"Last week was significantly colder than the week before, so I'm looking for a pretty healthy draw," said one Houston-based trader.
Last week's decline of 22 bcf surprised most players who expected stocks to be flat or up slightly.
Weekly drawdowns in November 1995 averaged 74 bcf.

In last report, Eastern stocks, remained at 96 percent of capacity, slightly above year-ago. Producing region inventories slipped slightly to 73 percent full and continued to seriously lag 1995 levels of about 85 percent of capacity.

For the same week last year, total inventories fell by 75 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would narrow the gap to 1995 to about 165 bcf. In 1995, eastern storage fell by 62 bcf, while producing stocks dropped by 25 bcf.
